title: Seal Cracking from Thermal Expansion Mismatch
introduction: The edge seal of a photovoltaic module bonds a cover plate to the module body using a sealant material. Because the thermal expansion coefficients of these two components differ, every temperature cycle causes them to expand and contract by different amounts. This repeated dimensional mismatch applies cyclic stress to the adhesive bond at the cover-sealant interface. After sufficient cycles of heating and cooling, the accumulated fatigue damage causes adhesive failure between the sealing rubber and the cover plate, initiating cracks in the edge seal that compromise the module's moisture barrier.
reasoning: The 1564-SPIE accelerated durability study directly attributes edge seal adhesive failure to mismatched thermal expansion coefficients between the cover plate and sealant under repeated temperature cycling.

key_findings.claim: Mismatched thermal expansion coefficients between cover plate and sealant cause adhesive failure after repeated heat-expansion/shrinkage cycles
key_findings.detail: The thermal expansion coefficient of the module cover plate and the sealant material differ. Over many cycles of heat expansion and shrinkage, this mismatch generates cyclic stress at the cover-sealant bond, ultimately causing adhesive failure between the sealing rubber and the cover plate.
